verdictReason: No edge. Review-before-submit and low price are already offered free or cheap: DisputePack has a free plan, Chargeback Copilot gives 3 free evidence PDFs a month, Chargeback Protector charges $4.99 a report, ChargebackWiz lets the merchant review and submit; Shopify pre-fills the evidence form natively and Stripe bills Smart Disputes only on a win. At least six such Shopify listings launched Jan-Aug 2026. Tiny stores gain little at $9, Shopify review/PCD is a real gate, and pessimistic year-1 profit is about -$250.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: Several. DisputePack (Shopify listing, launched 2026-08-21) has a free plan with AI rebuttal drafts and PDF evidence packs; its listing summary says the merchant reviews, edits and submits. Chargeback Copilot has a free tier of 3 evidence PDFs/month, then $19/month. Chargeback Protector charges $4.99 per generated report, first report free, no subscription. Evidkit is $29/month and drafts for merchant approval. ChargebackWiz lets the merchant 'review and submit in one click' and charges 18% only on recovered chargebacks. Shopify itself auto-populates the chargeback response form and sends it on the due date. Stripe Smart Disputes bills a fee only if you win and auto-submit can be turned off. ChargePay is flat $19.99-$99.99. A flat $9 packet builder with review adds nothing these do not already offer at $0-$29.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None. Price ($9) and a review step are the only differences and are product settings, not exclusive assets: any of the six 2026 entrants (incl. Paidback, 15% capped at $250, launched 2026-05-11) or ChargePay can add a review toggle or a cheaper tier in one release, and Shopify/Stripe are bundling native tooling. No exclusive data (win-rate history, processor access) is available to a stranger with $10k. Possible compounding asset would be a Shopify app-store review base, but incumbents (e.g. ChargePay, listed since 2020 with a 4.5 rating from 27 reviews on the fetched page) already hold it. Falsifier: evidence that merchant-reviewed packets win materially more than auto-built packets AND that rivals refuse to add review; none found, and the reverse is observed.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: Merchants with enough disputes pay: ChargePay flat $19.99-$99.99/month (no success fee), Chargeflow 25% and Disputifier 20% (capped $250) of recoveries (case-file evidence E1-E2). A roundup says ChargePay at $19.99 pays back once you recover one or two chargebacks a month and that smaller stores often cannot justify setup cost for heavier tools. There is no evidence that stores with a handful of disputes a month pay anything for a packet builder, and several free options exist. At $9/month ($108/year) a store must recover roughly two extra disputes a year (assuming about $50-65 each incl. the $15 fee; assumption), but Shopify already pre-fills evidence free, so the marginal win uplift of a $9 builder is unproven.

answers.question: (4) Legal / platform constraints?
answers.answer: Shopify App Store review is a gate: one developer reports a posted 8-10 day SLA but no update for over 30 days after submission (submitted Jan 2026, posted Mar 2026); the same thread reports a rejection caused by a reviewer misreading a support email link. Reading customer name/address/email requires protected-customer-data Level 2 access: data-protection details, encryption, access logging, incident response policy, and Shopify may request a detailed review. Shopify Payments disputes are handled in the Shopify admin; apps submit or package evidence under card-network deadlines and cannot promise outcomes. Fee refund on a win is Shopify's rule, not the app's. Anonymous entrant handling payment/customer data is a trust problem for a 0-review app. Stripe and PayPal APIs add further integration and review work.

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers (reference entrant: $500, 11 h/week, first revenue day 45)?
answers.answer: Base case (all inputs assumptions except price): live and paid from month 3 (allowing for the reported 30+ day review), 2 paying merchants at end of month 3 growing by 3 a month to 29 at month 12 = 155 merchant-months x $9 = $1,395 revenue. Cash cost $539 (hosting/email $180, domain/site $30, partner/listing fee $19 assumption, legal templates/DPA $250, monitoring $60) = profit about $856 for roughly 570 owner hours (about $1.5/hour). Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5): revenue $558, cost $808.50, profit about -$250.50. Does not survive. Support effort per dispute and any manual review labour are not priced.

killReasons.reason: The only differences (flat low price, merchant review before submit) are already offered free or at $0-$29 by multiple live Shopify listings (DisputePack free plan, ChargebackWiz, Evidkit, Chargeback Copilot, Chargeback Protector), plus Shopify's native pre-filled form and Stripe's win-only Smart Disputes. At least six of these launched Jan-Aug 2026, so any rival can also copy or undercut a $9 offer in one release. No exclusive or compounding asset exists.

Pessimistic year-1 economics are negative (about -$250 on about $558 revenue) and the base case is about $856 for roughly 570 owner hours. Target stores with a handful of disputes per month have little to gain: heavier flat-fee tools are justified only by stores with more than a few disputes, and Shopify already pre-fills evidence free.

Distribution/trust gate for an anonymous solo entrant: Shopify App Store review reported at 30+ days against a posted 8-10 day SLA, and customer name/address/email requires protected-customer-data approval with Level 2 security controls and a possible detailed review. A 0-review app handling payment/customer data competes with listings that already have reviews.

legalNotes: Shopify App Store review is mandatory for a public listing; the review page gives no timeframe, a developer reports 30+ days against an 8-10 day SLA.

Access to customer name, address, phone or email needs protected-customer-data approval; Level 2 requires encrypted backups, separated test/production data, access logs, staff-access limits and an incident response policy, and Shopify may run a detailed data protection review.
Merchants and apps cannot promise dispute outcomes; the issuer decides, and merchants in network dispute resolution programs cannot contest (case-file evidence E8).
Processing payment and customer data as an anonymous entrant creates privacy-law and contract exposure; privacy policy and merchant data processing agreement are needed (Level 1 requirement).
